value.hook: When adding TTL-based not-found or unknown caching, especially PA size reads or another consumer that caches completed results.
value.title: Negative-cache expiry must survive consumer caches

sections.name: body
sections.value:
A source TTL does not bound staleness when a consumer never asks again. In #249 R249-001, the adapter correctly expired a 30-second transcript miss, but PA refresh_sizes classified NotFound as a completed CachedSize { tokens: None, stale: false }. A whole first turn could finish between PA rounds; the next idle read consumed the kept miss at its final activity generation, then the unchanged idle seat was skipped forever. The adapter-only expiry tests all passed.

The minimal repair marks only NotFound retryable on the existing PA round. Unbound/Unsupported stay completed; successful unchanged idle seats remain cached. This adds at most one size-refresh call per missing seat per minute, no new timer or idle-fleet reread. Unknown sizes neither cross nor rearm large-seat claims, so these retries do not spam FYIs.

The decisive regression uses the real adapter: prime a miss, create a 700k transcript, let the PA read inside the miss lifetime, expire it, then require a large-seat notice on the next round with NO further activity. A separate adapter case pins same-seat target changes and clearing the old miss after a hit. R249-001 closed at cbe6a01d; reviewer output cb58e105.

For #251, keep cache scope honest: HeldProjection retains metadata per EVER-carded SeatId until restart, not merely current live seats. It preserves the former full seat-history fold; clearing a cache on rebinding alone would replay the same old holds, not establish incarnation isolation. Final reviewer output 89758d61 at 6ed8f1f7.

magicWand: make real-source consumer-expiry fixtures the default for negative-cache changes. difficulties: a source-level TTL test cannot reveal a downstream cache that stops reading altogether; distinguish source freshness from consumer convergence.
